analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: Knowing WHEN the PBC engine writes is not knowing WHAT it decides. HUNCALC0 turns HR position and employee data into FM earmarked-funds commitments (FMRESERV) — the rules of that conversion are the AS-DESIGNED half of the domain and we hold none of it. Read the engine: what drives the amount, which period it commits to, how a position change re-drives an existing reservation, and what ZPBC_PERIOD_CLS_EXEC does at close. This is the A_PROCESS cell, and it is the largest write path in the installation.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: extract HUNCALC0 / RHRFPM_ENGINE_* / ZPBC_PERIOD_CLS_EXEC source from D01 via ADT; trace against FMRESERV rows for one position across two months
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: Five decision rules read from production source and integrated into normative_models.POST2BUDGET as checkable rules. Biennium gap closed.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: The largest write path in the installation is operated through ONE NAMED USER account (F_DERAKHSHAN, 74.1% of all change documents) rather than a service account, and ZPBC_PERIOD_CLS_EXEC has exactly one operator. Two separate issues follow: a SINGLE POINT OF DEPENDENCE — if that person is unavailable, the monthly commitment run has no second operator — and an ATTRIBUTION problem: every FM commitment posting is recorded against a person, so the change log cannot distinguish an engine run from a manual edit by that user. State it as an observation with the measurement attached; the remedy (service account, second operator) is the tenant's decision, not ours.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: cross-check against the E_AUTH cell and the H71 write-channel SoD finding

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: A8 became SLOW when the channel evidence was added, and slow is a correctness problem here, not a comfort one: three heavy passes were added over the audit log — two LIKE scans for file paths and a PARAMX GROUP BY over 8.7M rows — none of which can use an index, and the golden database is read-only by contract so an index cannot be added. The run went from roughly 3 minutes to over 15. The D6 lesson applies directly: A SLOW ALGORITHM GETS SKIPPED, AND A SKIPPED ALGORITHM IS DOCUMENTATION — and A8 now sits inside the analysis cycle, so it slows every cycle for every domain.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: apply pattern D6 properly: ONE pass over rsau_audit_history that emits every signal at once (program, RFC flag, file flag, caller) grouped by (user, day, hour), instead of four separate scans. Then cache the aggregate against MAX(SAL_DATE) exactly as detect_drift does, so a re-run with no new audit data costs nothing.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: A8 runs in the cycle; its cost is paid on every domain, every time.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: >1h -> 3m29s. 15.6M audit rows collapsed to 987K indexed slots and 12M change rows to 507K groups, in a DERIVED database — the golden is 13 GB, gitignored and unbacked, so it cannot be indexed in place.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: A8 went from ~3 minutes to over 10 when the FILE and ORIGIN evidence was added. The origin query parses PARAMX across 8.7M rows and the file query scans PARAM3 with four LIKE patterns, neither of which is cached. By our own D6 principle this matters more than it looks: a slow algorithm gets skipped, and a skipped algorithm is documentation — which is exactly the state A8 was built to rescue other algorithms from. Apply the same fix D6 got: cache the aggregate against the newest SAL_DATE watermark, so a re-run with no new audit data costs nothing.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: watermark cache alongside the tool, as in detect_drift.build_profile()

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: 37 objects of package ZPBC exist in D01 and NOT in P01, including SIXTEEN transactions (ZPBC_CIPE_ANALYSIS, ZPBC_COMPLETION, ZPBC_PERIOD_BLOCK, ZPBC_SET_CHKAC and others) plus 5 tables and 3 BAdI implementations. Either they are unreleased development, or they were deliberately not transported, or they are abandoned. Each answer means something different for the domain: unreleased work is a pending change, abandoned work is debt, and deliberately-dev-only tooling is a support pattern. Determine which by checking the transport history (E070/E071) for those objects.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: compare TADIR ZPBC D01 vs P01, then read E070/E071 for the 37

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: The authored rule P2B-3 assumes a 'declared vacancy tolerance' — a limit on how long a vacant post may hold a commitment. No such tolerance is visible in the encumbrance code read so far. What bounds the commitment is MV_EXTENSION_YEARS = 10, which is a HORIZON, not a tolerance. Determine whether a vacancy tolerance exists elsewhere (customizing, another BAdI, or the requirement filter classes) or whether the authored rule describes an intent the system does not implement. Either answer is a finding.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: read ZCL_IM__UNESCO_ENCUMB_VACANCY and the ZIF_REQUIREMENT_VAC_HANDLING chain
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: no tolerance exists. P2B-3 states an intent the system does not implement — a vacant post holds its commitment for the whole funding window.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: MV_EXTENSION_YEARS = 10 rests on a stated assumption with an expiry: 'no contract end date will exceed 3 years from today' (Spring 2019). Nothing in the system monitors whether that still holds. Count PA0001/PA0016 contract end dates beyond today + 10 years, and beyond today + 3, and take the result to the business. A business rule frozen in a constant with an expiring justification is the definition of a silent risk.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: read PA0016/PA0001 end dates from P01 and compare against the constant
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: safe today, premise false: 16 real dates beyond +3y, 0 beyond +10y, furthest 20310831. The 1,335 at HIGHDATE are indefinite contracts, not long terms.
